title: Machine-learning based prediction models for Parkinson’s disease and atypical Parkinsonian disorders from advanced neuroimaging
summary:
Idiopathic Parkinson’s syndrome (iPS), the second most common neurodegenerative disease, is of great importance in our increasingly aging society. Diagnosis is typically based on characteristic motor symptoms; however, neurological assessment can be challenging. Atypical Parkinsonian syndromes (aPS), such as progressive supranuclear gaze palsy (PSP), multiple system atrophy (MSA), corticobasal syndrome (CBS), and even Wilson disease (WD), can mimic the motor symptoms of iPS, making accurate differentiation difficult.
In recent years, advanced brain imaging techniques have identified disease-specific changes in the brain across various disorders, offering the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy. The goal of this project is to enhance the diagnosis of patients with different movement disorders by leveraging these advancements.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Neurologically diagnosed idiopathic Parkinson's disease, an atypical parkinsonian syndrome, or diagnosed Wilson disease.
Healthy subjects, matched for age and gender to atypical parkinsonian disease and Wilson disease patients.
Exclusion criteria:
MRI contraindication (e.g. metal implants, claustrophobia), other neuropsychiatric diseases (e.g. dementia etc.), pregnancy and breastfeeding.
